questionTexts:
? Yes — the sheet lists Persuasion at +7 (Charisma +4 plus proficiency from Beguiling Influence). Success stands, thank you.

"Three tendays. And they all sat." I nod to Mirela, and I keep my hands where they are. "Then I'm the first who didn't, and that's worth knowing. The drink's yours — ask for it under my name at the Elfsong, not the house red."

I turn and walk up to Tamsin, Copper still riding my shoulder, and fall in beside her as we climb toward Windspell Street. Quietly, once we're clear of the crates: "You've carried packs on this quay a while. A copper coin with a wheel on it, cut clean in half through the hub — that mean anything to you? Whose mark is it?"

? The sheet does list it — under "James's Papers": "a pay slip of Queen Zaranda's regiment with a signature; a promissory note… ; a letter from his old company that he never finished reading." The sheet leaves the contents to you. What I know as the player: the company was the second one, the one that lost the old warlock in the Nashkel mines, the one whose rod James carries. He opened the letter the night before that last hand, read the first page, and put it away — he'd tell you he was interrupted, but really he didn't want to know what they wanted of him. Who wrote it and what it says are yours. I'll read it next turn, in character.
